Single-axis follow-up to the rejected VK128 padded direct-F32 Q4_K WMMA probe. It preserves BM128/BN128/BK32/WG256, direct F32 RHS, and Vulkan's 40-half padded LDS stride, but explicitly prefetches both k-half A/B LDS fragments for each output tile before issuing WMMA. This moves the HIP lowering toward RADV's deeper LDS-load-before-WMMA cadence while staying wave32 because the ROCm WMMA builtin rejects wave64 compilation.

Exact-schedule follow-up to the rejected VK128 padded direct-F32 Q4_K WMMA probes. RADV-ISA-driven follow-up to the rejected wave64 VK128 padded direct-F32 Q4_K WMMA route. It preserves BM128/BN128/BK32/WG256, direct F32 RHS, Vulkan's 40-half padded LDS stride, the ROCm wave64 WMMA builtin, and the same OPSEL/store policy, but spells LDS fragment reads as half4 chunks to target the RADV b64-style LDS feed rather than the existing HIP route's coalesced ds_load_b128 fragment loads. It is rejected at the compile/ISA gate: non-volatile half4 source coalesced back to the existing ds_load_b128 pattern (32 ds_load_b128, 0 ds_load_b64, 32 WMMA, 155 waits, SGPR=29, VGPR=165, LDS=20480), while a volatile spelling emitted flat_load_b64 with immediate vmcnt waits, raised VGPR to 233, and dropped to 28 static WMMA sites. Keep it opt-in only as evidence that C++ half4 source spelling is not enough to recover RADV's ds_load_b64 schedule.

RADV-ISA-driven follow-up to the rejected wave64 VK128 padded half4 source probe. It preserves BM128/BN128/BK32/WG256, direct F32 RHS, Vulkan's 40-half padded LDS stride, the ROCm wave64 WMMA builtin, and the same OPSEL/store policy, but uses explicit ds_read_b64 inline assembly for A/B LDS fragment reads. It is rejected after focused correctness: the route emitted LDS ds_load_b64 and selected correctly for p512/p513 while p33 stayed on the narrow route, but p512 and p513 CPU-reference rows failed. Adding a memory clobber to the inline read changed the failure from NaN/inf to finite ERR around 0.006-0.012 on p512 and 0.0016-0.0118 on p513, proving optimizer visibility matters, but direct half4 asm output, conservative s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0) after each read, and explicit address_space(3) base-pointer arithmetic still did not pass correctness. The final emitted schedule has 256 ds_load_b64, 0 ds_load_b128, 32 WMMA, 396 waits, SGPR=30, VGPR=169, LDS=20480. Keep it opt-in only as evidence that forced ds_load_b64 is possible, but this fragment spelling is not semantically equivalent to the RADV schedule.

RADV-ISA-driven follow-up to the rejected wave64 VK128 padded B64ASM diagnostic. It preserves BM128/BN128/BK32/WG256, direct F32 RHS, Vulkan's 40-half padded LDS stride, the ROCm wave64 WMMA builtin, OPSEL/store policy, and explicit ds_read_b64 LDS fragment reads, but changes the compute window to load four A fragments and four B fragments for each k-half, wait, then issue the 4x4 WMMA block. The no-wait grouping emitted the target 64 ds_load_b64 / 32 WMMA shape but failed focused p512/p513 correctness with NaNs. The conservative waited grouping still emitted 64 ds_load_b64, 0 ds_load_b128, 32 WMMA, 206 waits, SGPR=29, VGPR=199, LDS=20480, no spills, and passed focused p512, p33, and p513 CPU-reference gates while selecting only p512/p513. It is rejected for production promotion because same-row Kcur p512 perf regressed badly versus current MMQL128: 1038.69 us -> 3103.19 us. Keep it opt-in as evidence that matching RADV's LDS load count and fragment reuse is not sufficient while the HIP inline-asm wait schedule remains far from RADV.
